title: Remote earthquake count asymmetry showed no clear change from hours 0-6 to hours 6-24 around 286 isolated M7+ events in 2000-2025
abstract: We tested whether remote count asymmetry changed between hours 0-6 and hours 6-24 around 286 isolated M7+ earthquakes in ComCat in 2000-2025. Targets had preferred M from 5.5 to below 6.5 and distance above 2,000 km. Early windows had 53 after counts and 76 before counts. Late windows had 205 after counts and 198 before counts. The early-minus-late rate contrast was -0.354 counts per center per day. Its conditional 95% year bootstrap interval was -0.808 to +0.116. The two-sided annual sign-flip p value was 0.164. Thus the primary test did not resolve a time contrast. A stronger M7.5+ subset contrast did not pass adjustment for five secondary tests. This direct test uses disjoint windows; it does not infer recovery from nested cumulative counts. It follows a prior campaign signal and uses the same source and centers. Sparse counts, event selection, mixed magnitudes and annual uncertainty assumptions limit inference. The results do not identify detection loss, physical suppression or recovery time. Code, annual aggregates, source hashes, a figure and an independent count audit support reproduction. Raw and event-level records remain external.

display.caption: Early and late count asymmetry and their direct contrast. Error bars are conditional 95% calendar-year bootstrap intervals. Secondary tests are unadjusted in the figure.

citations.reason: Same source and isolated centers. We directly test the early-to-late asymmetry difference that nested windows could not establish.
Prior five-day low-count contrast uses overlapping source data and a different endpoint.
